low-energy recoil defects caused by proton irradiation of AlGaln/Gan high-electron-mobilty transistors are more likely than atomic displacements to occur in a defect-free crystal and that these low-energy recoil defects cause threshold-voltage shifts and 1/f-noise increases.

radiation-induced defect evolution and electrical degradation of AlGaN/ GaN high-electron-mo-bility transistors (HEMTs) is due to displacement cascades in the AlGaN barrier layer, which are mediated by the presence of defect complexes.
low-energy recoil defects are responsible for the radiation-induced degradation of the AlGaN/GaNNHEM Ts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the radiation-induced defects and the electrical degradation of AlGaN/ GaN high-electron mobility transistors.
the development of a comprehensive model for the radiation-induced defect evolution and electrical degradation of AlGaN/ GaN high-electron-momentum transistors (HEMTs).
understanding the mechanisms of radiation damage in AlGaN/GaNs high-electron-momentum transistors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the displacement damage mechanism is defect-mediated.
the defect complexes, such as Ga vacancy and Al interstitial, are responsible for the radiation-induced degradation of AlGaN/ GaN HEMTs.
radiation-induced defect evolution and electrical degradation are the result of low-energy recoil processes in AlGaN/GaNs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radiation-induced defects in GaN-based HEMTs are the main source of the degradation of the device performance.
we have identified the defect precursors and responsible defect complexes in the displacement damage mechanism in proton irradiation of AlGn/GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs).
the radiation-induced degradation in AlGaN/GAN HEMT devices can be understood as the evolution of defects from the as-grown state to the irradiated state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
radiation-induced defects can be a major source of electrical degradation in AlGaN/Gan high-electron-mo-bility transistors.
low-energy recoiled defects are the main contributors to device degradation.
radiation damage in semiconductors can occur via defect-mediated displacement mechanisms, which may lead to new strategies to mitigate radiation damage in semiconductor devices.
